title: The Principal a Certificate of Deposit Term Has Lost
content:
The principal a term of a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line has lost is measured against the owner's borrowing and against how often principal has left the certificate.

## The measure

The principal the term has lost is measured as follows: where the owner has an auto loan at the bank that is not past due and principal was taken out of the certificate more than once in the twelve months before the deposit, it is the principal those withdrawals removed together with every entry booked for them in those months, less any credit back posted in them; where the owner has an auto loan at the bank that is not past due and principal was taken out only once in those months, it is the principal that withdrawal removed together with every entry booked for it in those months; in every other case, whatever loans the owner has and however often principal was taken out, it is the principal taken out by early partial withdrawals in those months, less any credit back posted in them.

## What is read

The loan is one of the bank's Auto Loans, and what is asked of it is whether it stands as not past due. The window is the twelve months before the deposit, and three things are read over it on the certificate's own ledger: the principal taken out by early partial withdrawals, the entries booked against those withdrawals, and any credit back posted to the certificate.

## Condition and result

| The owner's auto loan | Times principal was taken out in those twelve months | The loss |
|---|---|---|
| held, not past due | more than once | the principal removed, together with every entry booked for them, less any credit back posted |
| held, not past due | once | the principal removed, together with every entry booked for it |
| held, not past due | none | the principal removed, less any credit back posted |
| past due, or none held | any | the principal removed, less any credit back posted |

The second grade is the one that leaves the credits back out: where principal left the certificate just once and the owner's loan stands as not past due, the entries booked are added and nothing is taken away.

## Worked readings, on hypothetical figures

Over the twelve months before the deposit, 9000.00 USD of principal was taken out across two early partial withdrawals, 260.00 USD was booked against them in entries, and 500.00 USD was credited back.

| The owner's borrowing | Times principal left | The loss |
|---|---|---|
| an auto loan not past due | twice | 8760.00 USD, being 9000.00 plus 260.00 less 500.00 |
| an auto loan past due | twice | 8500.00 USD, being 9000.00 less 500.00 |
| no auto loan | twice | 8500.00 USD |

Where the same 9000.00 USD had left in a single withdrawal, with 260.00 USD booked against it and 500.00 USD credited back, an owner with an auto loan not past due would show a loss of 9260.00 USD, the credit back being left out of that grade.
